commit_message: GATE-03: secure authenticated directed links — 3-message transcript-bound handshake
scope_completed: ADR-0016 updated from PROPOSAL to RESOLVED (Principal Architect approved via roadmap §B frozen protocol decisions)
3-message authenticated handshake implemented in reference/transport/auth-handshake.ts per the frozen spec
Transcript hash: BLAKE3-256 with u32be length-prefixed message framing per SHARENET/LINK/TRANSCRIPT/1
Possession payload: domain_tag || transcript_hash || link_id_bytes || peer_challenge || role_byte
Each party signs the challenge generated by the peer (never its own)
LINK_UP exists only after both proofs verify; ADV_VERIFIED is not routable
ChallengeCache with 5-minute expiration + single-use + replay rejection
5 ratified conformance vectors: valid, tampered, replayed, wrong-role, wrong-LinkId
TS and Python verifiers both pass 14/14 vectors (cross-language conformance)
protocol_adr_references: ADR-0014 (LinkId derivation + two-message handshake — superseded by auth-handshake for LINK_UP)
known_limitations: Real TCP integration (mini-service update to use the 3-message handshake) is deferred to a follow-up commit. The current mini-service still uses the 2-message ADV_VERIFIED exchange. The integration test (test:integration:mesh) currently tests ADV_VERIFIED, not LINK_UP.

The challenge cache is in-memory only (no persistence across restarts). This is acceptable for the handshake (challenges expire in 5 minutes) but a production implementation should use a shared cache for multi-process deployments.

LinkId derivation still uses BLAKE2b-256 (reference/link/link.ts). A follow-up should update it to BLAKE3-256 for consistency with the NodeId derivation, but this does not affect the handshake correctness since LinkId is derived identically by both parties.
